history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN (DIGAMBARA) TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. TOWN CORRECTED: the CSV lists 'Rajgir', but the Nandyavarta (Nandyawart Mahal) Jain temple complex is at Kundalpur village near Nalanda, about 12-15 km from Rajgir; Kundalpur (Nalanda district) is the correct town. Coordinates (25.148, 85.444639) are from Wikipedia for the Kundalpur Jain temple, not the map geocoder (rate-limited); web-corroborated, not field-verified. Kundalpur is regarded in the Digambara tradition as the birthplace of Mahavira (the 24th Tirthankara) — though modern scholarship and other Jain traditions identify his birthplace (Kundagrama) with Basukund near Vaishali, so the birthplace claim is disputed. Kundalpur was an ancient Licchavi capital and is also believed to be the birthplace of Gautama Swami, Mahavira's chief disciple. The present seven-storey Nandyavart palace complex (6 temples) was built in just 22 months in 2003-2004 under the inspiration of Gyanmati Mataji: a 101-ft Mahavira temple with an 11-ft standing idol, Rishabhdev Jinmandir, Navgraha Shanti Jinmandir, Trikal Choubisi Jinmandir (72 Tirthankara idols), and a Shantinath shrine on the topmost floor. Governing body: Bhagwan Mahavira Janmabhoomi Kundalpur Digambar Jain Samiti.

name: Nandyavarta Jain Temple
town_description: Kundalpur is a village near Nalanda in Nalanda district, Bihar, about 1.6 km from the ruins of the Nalanda mahavihara. An ancient Licchavi capital, it is revered in the Digambara Jain tradition as the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, and as the birthplace of Gautama Swami, his first disciple; an older ancient Jain temple also survives beside the modern complex.
